title: I've Known Omar Since University
title_ar: أنا أعرف عمر من أيام الجامعة
gist_ar: خطاب فرح ودّي على السطح. تحت السطح فيه اعتراض واعتذار. كله بالأسلوب.

before_listening.en: A best man's speech. Warm on the surface. Underneath it there is both a reproach and an apology, and neither is stated.
before_listening.ar: خطاب صاحب العريس. ودود من برّه. جوّاه عتاب واعتذار، والاتنين مش مقولين صريح.

segments.speaker: Best man
segments.text: Right. Phones down, I'll be quick, and I've been asked by three separate people not to mention Prague, so I won't mention Prague. I've known Omar since university, which is nineteen years, and in that time I have watched him become extremely good at one specific thing, which is being the person everybody rings. You all know this. You've all rung him. Some of you rang him this week about the seating. He is the man who turns up with a van. He turned up with a van for me in 2016 and he has never once mentioned it since, which is the part I'd draw your attention to, because most people would have got two years out of that story. And I want to say something to Leila, who I met four years ago and who I liked immediately, and who I'll admit I was slightly wary of for about six months, entirely on Omar's behalf and entirely unnecessarily. Leila, you are the first person I have seen ring him and ask him nothing. You ask him how he is. And you wait. It's an extraordinary thing to watch, if you've known him as long as I have, because he doesn't know what to do with the pause and he's learning. Now. There's a version of this speech where I list his flaws for laughs, and I've written it, and it's funnier than this one. But I'd rather use my ninety seconds on this: Omar, you spent most of your thirties being useful to people, and a few of us let you, and I let you more than most. I've thought about that a fair bit this year. So my toast isn't to the happy couple, if you'll forgive me, because you'll get plenty of those. It's to the next nineteen years being the ones where somebody turns up with a van for you. And Leila already has. To Omar and Leila.

gist_question.q: What is the speaker admitting about himself in this speech?
options: That he was jealous of Leila when they first met
That he had forgotten to prepare a speech until that morning
That he no longer sees Omar as often as he used to
That he took advantage of Omar's willingness to help and did so more than others

questions.q: Why does he draw attention to Omar never mentioning the van in 2016?
options: To show Omar does not trade on the things he does for people
To suggest Omar has a poor memory and has genuinely forgotten the favour
To explain why he owes Omar money
To hint that the favour was never actually completed

questions.q: What does he praise Leila for specifically?
options: Organising the seating plan for the wedding, which everyone had been ringing Omar about
Persuading Omar to travel more
Ringing Omar to ask him how he is, and asking him for nothing
Introducing Omar to his current job

questions.q: What is the effect of mentioning that he wrote a funnier speech and discarded it?
options: It apologises in advance for the speech being dull
It implies the funnier version insulted Leila
It signals that what follows is deliberately chosen sincerity, not inability to be funny
It fills time while he finds his notes

questions.q: What is the toast at the end actually wishing for?
options: That Omar becomes the one who is helped rather than only the helper
That the couple move closer to their friends
That Omar becomes less available to the people who ring him
That the next nineteen years are quieter than the last

questions.q: What does 'I've been asked by three separate people not to mention Prague' achieve?
options: It sets up a joke he later returns to and completes
It explains why several guests could not attend
It signals that the speech will be entirely improvised
It raises a story and withholds it, while showing he can be trusted with it

glossary.word: get two years out of a story
